Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component, its main parts, and their relationships. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title
|
|-- First component
|   `-- Supporting detail
`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Ghostty core: Surface - one interactive terminal session (src/Surface.zig)
|
|-- Runtime boundary and application context
|   |-- src/apprt.zig: runtime.App / runtime.Surface
|   |   |-- Compile-time adapters: GTK executable, embedded library, browser
|   |   `-- Runtime supplies UI events and window/tab/split placement;
|   |       Surface exposes callbacks without owning that UI hierarchy
|   |-- src/App.zig: surfaces, focused_surface, mailbox
|   |   `-- Registers sessions and routes surface messages/config updates
|   |-- App.font_grid_set / App.device
|   |   `-- Shared font grids and graphics device; Surface retains a grid reference
|   `-- Surface.rt_app.performAction() / rt_surface.close()
|       `-- Delegates native UI actions and close confirmation to the runtime
|
|-- Session coordination and input (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- Public entry points: keyCallback(), textCallback(), mouseButtonCallback(),
|   |   cursorPosCallback(), scrollCallback(), focusCallback(), preeditCallback()
|   |   `-- Maintains keyboard, mouse, focus, visibility and IME/preedit state
|   |-- performBindingAction() -> local terminal action or rt_app.performAction()
|   |   `-- Shortcuts can consume input instead of sending it to the child
|   |-- Private encodeKey() / encodeKeyOpts(); src/input/key_encode.zig,
|   |   src/input/mouse_encode.zig
|   |   `-- Encoding depends on current Terminal modes, not just the UI event
|   |-- Private queueIo() -> Termio.queueMessage() -> termio.Thread
|   |   `-- Transfers message ownership; readonly blocks PTY writes
|   `-- selectionString(), completeClipboardRequest(), search, inspector
|       `-- Selection/copy/paste, search and inspection use the same session state
|
|-- Child process and byte transport (Surface.io / io_thread)
|   |-- src/termio/Termio.zig: Termio
|   |   `-- Owns backend, terminal, terminal_stream, mailbox and DerivedConfig
|   |-- src/termio/Exec.zig: Exec / Subprocess
|   |   `-- Owns PTY and child command lifecycle, environment and shell integration
|   |-- src/termio/Thread.zig: threadMain(), mailbox handling
|   |   `-- Write messages -> Termio.queueWrite() -> Exec.queueWrite() -> PTY
|   |-- Exec.ReadThread -> Termio.processOutput()
|   |   `-- PTY output: gather buffers -> reader/parser; Windows uses a serial loop
|   `-- src/apprt/surface.zig: Message / Mailbox
|       `-- Child exit and terminal UI requests -> App.surfaceMessage()
|           -> Surface.handleMessage() -> runtime actions or session state changes
|
|-- Terminal emulation and authoritative content (Termio.terminal)
|   |-- Termio.processOutput() -> terminal_stream.nextSlice()
|   |   |-- src/terminal/stream.zig: Stream; Parser.zig / UTF8Decoder.zig
|   |   |   `-- Turns incoming bytes into decoded text and VT actions
|   |   `-- src/termio/stream_handler.zig: StreamHandler.vt() / vtPrintAscii()
|   |       `-- Updates Terminal, queues protocol replies and requests rendering/UI work
|   |-- src/terminal/Terminal.zig: Terminal
|   |   |-- Renderer-independent grid operations: print, cursor movement, erase, resize
|   |   `-- Owns screens, modes, colors, tabstops, scrolling region, title and pwd
|   `-- Terminal.screens -> src/terminal/ScreenSet.zig
|       |-- Primary screen plus lazily created alternate screen; tracks active screen
|       `-- src/terminal/Screen.zig: Screen
|           |-- Cursor, saved cursor, tracked selection, keyboard/image protocol state
|           `-- Screen.pages -> src/terminal/PageList.zig -> src/terminal/page.zig
|               `-- Ordered pages hold scrollback and active rows/cells;
|                   tracked pins keep viewport, cursor and selections attached to content
|
|-- Shared-state synchronization and presentation
|   |-- Surface.renderer_state: src/renderer/State.zig
|   |   |-- terminal = &Surface.io.terminal; also exposes preedit and mouse state
|   |   `-- Mutex protects referenced data, not a second copy of terminal content
|   |-- Termio.processOutput() locks shared state and schedules a render
|   |   `-- State.lockDemand() / unlockDemand() / yieldToDemand()
|   |       prevent continuous output parsing from starving frame snapshots
|   |-- Surface.renderer_thread: src/renderer/Thread.zig
|   |   `-- Wakeups/timers/mailbox -> Renderer.updateFrame() -> drawFrame()
|   |-- src/renderer/generic.zig: Renderer
|   |   |-- updateFrame() snapshots Terminal into terminal.RenderState under lock
|   |   |-- font_grid + font_shaper + font_shaper_cache supply glyph layout
|   |   `-- drawFrame() turns prepared cells, colors, cursor and images into output
|   `-- src/renderer.zig: GenericRenderer(GraphicsAPI)
|       `-- Metal.zig or OpenGL.zig; uses App.device and runtime presentation surface
|
|-- Configuration and geometry connect input, emulator and renderer
|   |-- Surface.DerivedConfig / Termio.DerivedConfig / Renderer.DerivedConfig
|   |   `-- Retain subsystem-specific configuration rather than borrowing Config lifetime
|   |-- App.updateConfig() -> Surface.handleMessage(.change_config) -> updateConfig()
|   |   `-- Propagates live changes across the session
|   `-- Surface.sizeCallback() -> private resize(); contentScaleCallback(), setFontSize()
|       |-- Font metrics + pixel size + padding -> renderer.Size.grid()
|       `-- Resize messages -> Termio.resize() and renderer thread
|           `-- PTY dimensions and Terminal.resize() change under the shared mutex,
|               keeping child redraws consistent with the emulator's grid
|
`-- Resource lifetime is centered on Surface
    |-- src/Surface.zig: init()
    |   `-- References shared fonts; creates renderer, mutex, Termio/Exec and mailboxes;
    |       starts renderer and IO threads with pointers to the same session state
    |-- close() -> runtime close process -> deinit()
    `-- deinit()
        |-- Stops search, then stops/joins renderer and IO threads before freeing shared data
        |-- Deinitializes renderer before renderer-thread handles, then IO resources
        `-- Releases inspector, keyboard allocations, font reference, preedit, mutex and config"}
